title: Conditional multitenant rate limiter priority skew causing transient under-enforcement
text:
Conditional multitenant rate limiter priority skew causing transient under-enforcement

description:
Intermittent cases where per-key priority overrides combined with per-org and per-route policies result in transient under-enforcement (requests allowed when they should be throttled). Observed as short windows of elevated usage for a small set of tenants after shard reassignment and policy hot-reload. This ticket captures investigation, repro, short-term mitigation, and a long-term fix plan.

impact:
Transient over-allow for small number of tenants leading to underbilling and potential customer perception issues; visible as short-lived bursts up to ~2x expected throughput for affected keys. Affects hosted and dedicated clusters during rolling updates or instance restarts.

reproduction_steps:
1) Create two tenants T1 and T2 sharing a shard (sticky-shard assignment enabled).
2) Configure per-org policy: default priority = low, per-route quota = 1000/min.
3) Configure per-key override for a service key K1 belonging to T1: priority = high, burst credits = +200.
4) Start a steady stream of requests from T1 at near-quota rate; verify enforcement hitting quota windows.
5) Trigger a shard reassignment for one edge node (simulate instance bounce or maintenance) while simultaneously applying a policy hot-reload that changes route fallback behavior.
6) Observe a ~10-30s window where requests for K1 are allowed beyond quota; metrics show credits attributed to the wrong in-memory bucket and enforcement checks returning allow from fast-path cache.
7) Collect tracer spans and edge logs for the window; reproduce locally using the shard-reassignment harness and time-accelerated policy reloads.

logs_snapshot:
edge: allow decision fastpath: key=K1 shard=sh-23 cache_hit=true priority=high quota_window_id=2026-03-12T10:04:00Z
shard-reassign: lease=renewal failover->sh-27 old_owner=sh-23 new_owner=sh-27
policy-hot-reload: version=v2026-03-12-1 route-fallback=enabled
meter-commit: credits_applied target_bucket=org:T2:key:Kx unexpected=true amount=200

hypothesis:
A race between sticky-shard mapping update and policy hot-reload causes fast-path cache entries (priority and credit pointers) to be re-keyed incorrectly. Per-key overrides store a pointer to a tenant-scoped credit bucket; during reassignment we are dereferencing a stale pointer and applying credits to the wrong tenant's bucket. Enforcement uses the fast-path decision if cache present, so the wrong credits cause an allow where a deny should occur.

experiment_results:
Replayed the sequence in staging using the shard-reassign harness. With no policy reload the issue did not occur. When timed policy reload coincided with reassignment, we reproduced the over-allow consistently. Enabling stronger pointer validation (temporary patch) eliminated the over-allows in the harness.

root_cause:
Sticky-shard pointer (in-memory bucket reference) is validated only by shard id but not by tenant id during fast-path credit application. Policy hot-reload mutates the route/priority indices while a shard transfer copies pointers; combined these can produce a transient pointer that points at an unrelated tenant's bucket. Enforcement fast-path accepts the cache without full tenant-level validation.

mitigations:
Short-term patch deployed to staging: on fast-path cache hit, perform tenant-id validation on the cached credit pointer before applying credits. Also increased grace period on shard handoff to reduce overlap. Rolled patch to canary edge fleet.

rollout_plan:
1) Canary for 2 hours on low-traffic region with added telemetry (done). 2) Gradual ramp to 30% of traffic with continued trace sampling for next 24 hours. 3) Full rollout after 48 hours if no regressions. 4) Follow with a database reconciliation backfill job to detect credits misapplied in last 7 days and create accounting fixes if needed.

long_term_fix:
Refactor in-memory credit pointer representation to be immutable and namespaced by tenant+shard+route. Replace pointer dereference fast-path with a lightweight validation token check (versioned binder). Add unit and property tests for concurrent shard handoff + policy reload scenarios.

regression_test_plan:
Add deterministic concurrency tests to runtime-policy-simulator: combinations of shard reassignment, policy hot-reload, per-key overrides, and burst credit application. Add e2e test in CI harness that exercises rolling updates with randomized interleavings. Add a smoke check after canary verifying no over-allow traces in last 10 minutes.

notes:
PM (Aisha Kapoor): prioritize mitigation; billing reconciliation may be needed if misapplied credits persist beyond 24h.
Security (Rajiv Patel): no PII involved in pointers but ensure tracing does not expose tenant ids in public dashboards.
Observation: reproduces more reliably when policy reload contains route fallback toggles rather than pure priority edits.
